name: Direct Orientation Barrier Obstructions
description: Shows no direct additive, affine, or pumped measure globally orients the duplicating step. All listed tool fragments fail globally while context closures lift the barriers.

program.name: The Termination Axis
program.summary: The rule recΔ b s (δ n) → app s (recΔ b s n) copies its payload and consumes one counter; a direct measure orients it exactly when it ignores the payload and increases strictly with the counter, and the additive, affine, matrix, arctic, tropical and Knuth-Bendix families fail under their stated premises, with mutual cycles and higher-order sharing as variants. The proofs that succeed change the observer: the dependency-pair projection to the counter, nonlinear coupling, and the lexicographic and multiset path orders; seventy-six methods and a residual catalog record the verdicts as bookkeeping.

oneLine: No direct additive, affine, or pumped measure globally orients the duplicating step, while context closure preserves the failures and cross-coupled weights delimit the dominance hypotheses.
summary: Objects are step-duplicating schemas with base, successor, wrapper and duplicating recursor plus additive, affine, quadratic, max-plus, matrix and observer measures and global orientation of the step and its context closure. The question is whether a direct syntactic measure can decrease across the duplicating rule for all instantiations and hence globally orient the system. The main results are unconditional impossibilities for additive, affine, restricted-quadratic, max-plus and max-depth families together with conditional impossibilities for cross-term, multilinear, polynomial and WPO families under base boundedness or dominance hypotheses and for lexicographic orders under a positive tracked value. A grammar closure characterizes orientation as payload-blindness with strict counter response, canonical threshold and negative, sharing and zero-measure examples show the Archimedean, attainment, tree and positivity premises cannot be dropped, and a cross-coupled weight shows the three dominance premises are sharp. Every failure is packaged as an explicit barrier triple and checked certificate that refutes global orientation, all tool fragments with stated pumps or witnesses are blocked, and each root failure lifts through the identity context to the full context closure. Scope is tree semantics with first-order full rewriting and monotone direct observation, with sharing, binders, innermost restriction, co-orders, computability and quotients recorded as outside.
boundary: A payload-reading direct measure rises on the pumped wrapper chain past a threshold already attained by a recursor term, so strict decrease across the duplicating step is impossible. The obstruction is the attained threshold and unbounded wrapper growth, while the payload-blind counter projection that forgets wrapper mass does decrease and does orient. The barrier is located by threshold, pump-discharge and certificate theorems that turn each measure with stated unboundedness, pump, dominance or positivity hypothesis into a concrete triple refuting global orientation, with ordered-field, grammar and dominance-sharpness results marking where the hypotheses are needed.

conclusions.statement: For every schema S and every affine measure M over S, it is false that for all b s n in S, M.eval of wrap s of recur b s n is strictly below M.eval of recur b s of succ n.
For every schema S, ordered carrier K, field affine measure M over S K and delta in K with 0 below delta, it is false that M delta-orients the duplicating step.
For every schema S and every additive measure M over S, it is false that for all b s n in S, M.eval of wrap s of recur b s n is strictly below M.eval of recur b s of succ n.

For every schema S and every restricted-quadratic counter measure, max-plus measure, max-depth measure with positive wrap offset, or constructor-local max-plus evaluation at any offsets over S, it is false that evaluation strictly decreases across the duplicating step for all b s n.

Given cross-term boundedness at base for a cross-term quadratic measure, frozen base-point dominance for a bounded multilinear measure, and eventual frozen-base dominance for a bounded polynomial or WPO-direct measure, it is false that the measure strictly orients the duplicating step for all b s n.
For every grammar expression e, OrientsDupStep of e.eval holds iff PayloadBlind of e.eval and CounterStrict of e.eval both hold.

For all t k with canonical schema S and measure M, eval of wrap k of recur base k base below eval of recur base k of succ base holds iff k is below recur_counter times succ_bias plus succ_scale times c_base, so the inequality holds for k below t and fails for k equal to t.

For every schema certificate cert over S and every declared direct method over a system with its extracted certificate, global orientation by the stored evaluator and order fails on the duplicating relation and on the system.

If a measure with an order globally orients StepCtxFull then it globally orients the root step through the identity context, and in particular no affine compositional measure and no quadratic counter measure globally orients StepCtxFull.

For every grammar expression e, strict orientation of e.eval implies payload-blindness of e.eval, weak orientation implies payload-blindness, and if a vector measure orients under an order dominated by a scalarization equal to e.eval then e.eval is payload-blind, so a payload-reading scalarization blocks vector orientation.

For every system Sys and every additive, affine unbounded, cross-quadratic unbounded, or other listed direct and extended fragment with its stated unbounded, pump or dominance witnesses, evaluation does not globally orient Sys, and the joint direct, extended and matrix catalog holds together.

There are cross-term quadratic, multilinear and polynomial witnesses that each violate its dominance premise while the shared cross-coupled weight strictly orients the duplicating step for all b s n, so the three dominance premises are load-bearing.
It is false that every affine measure fails to be nonincreasing across the duplicating step, witnessed by the identically-zero affine measure whose nonincrease holds by definition.

In the strictly negative integer model every duplicating instance strictly decreases while no term attains the successor weight, and for all shared terms the sharing-aware counter strictly decreases across the shared step, so attainment and tree semantics are load-bearing.

openPoints: Cross-term quadratic barriers carry boundedness at base; multilinear barriers carry frozen base-point dominance; polynomial and WPO barriers carry eventual frozen-base dominance, and the cross-coupled weight shows each premise cannot be dropped.
Lexicographic, primary-first and scalar-dominance barriers carry a positive tracked value or unbounded range; without such positivity the statements give no claim.
Nonstrict affine barriers carry existence of a positive value; the identically-zero measure shows the premise cannot be dropped.
The ordered-field unbounded-range route carries an Archimedean hypothesis; lexicographic doubling in Nat times Nat stays below (1,0) and shows the route fails without it.
Ordered additive barriers carry attainment of the successor weight or nonnegativity of base weight; the negative-integer model shows attainment cannot be dropped.
Unrestricted nonlinear families without witnesses and matrix continuations outside stated pumps remain outside the barrier and are left open.

The barrier holds for tree semantics with first-order full rewriting and monotone direct observation; sharing, binders, innermost restriction, co-orders, computability and quotients lie outside scope.
Context-closed lifts add and drop no hypotheses through the identity-context embedding.

subTopics.name: Pump-discharge and scalar matrix depth barriers

files.summary: The file defines affine measures over an ordered semiring K with nonnegative values, wrapper coefficients at least one, and affine equations for base, successor, wrap and recursor. It defines Lucas delta-orientation and unbounded range, and proves wrap and doubling lower bounds. It proves that one positive value yields unbounded range under an Archimedean hypothesis, and proves a universal barrier: no affine measure delta-orients the duplicating step for any positive delta, via a threshold already attained by a recursor term. It instantiates the barrier for NNRat and NNReal by coercion and gives a lexicographic doubling example showing the unbounded-range route needs the Archimedean hypothesis.
files.conclusion: No affine measure over the stated ordered-semiring class delta-orients the duplicating step for any positive delta.

files.summary: The file defines a canonical schema over Nat whose recursor scales only the counter and a canonical affine measure whose generic contradiction bound equals t. It proves the bound specializes to t and that the distinguished root-step inequality is equivalent to k less than that bound. Below the bound the instance is strictly oriented and at the bound strict orientation fails, so the bound is attained and sharp.
files.conclusion: The canonical family attains the generic affine contradiction bound and shows it is an exact cutoff.

files.summary: This file defines decidable barrier classes and normalized coefficient tables for scalar and tracked-primary pair measures, with Boolean shape predicates and pump and bounded-regime checks. It provides conversions from additive, affine, restricted-quadratic, cross-term and matrix measures to those tables and classifiers reporting structural tags and pump flags. It proves additive tables carry all four nested tags, affine and restricted-quadratic tables carry tags according to their coefficients, every cross-term table carries the ambient cross-term tag, and pair conversions preserve componentwise versus lex order.
files.conclusion: Normalized coefficient tables are classified into nested additive, affine, restricted-quadratic and bounded cross-term tags and componentwise versus lex pair orders that select the structurally relevant barrier.

files.summary: This file specializes schema pump-discharge barriers to ko7Schema, ko7System and the duplicating step recDelta b s (delta n) to app s (recDelta b s n). It proves unconditional failure of global strict orientation for affine, restricted-quadratic, max-plus, arctic and tropical primary, componentwise vector and pair, functional and mixed measures. It proves conditional failure for cross-term quadratic, multilinear, polynomial and WPO-polynomial families under base-point boundedness or dominance, for lexicographic and scalar-dominance families under one positive tracked value, and for fixed-row and row-sum projections without pump assumptions.
files.conclusion: Every listed affine, quadratic, cross-term, multilinear, polynomial, max-plus, arctic, tropical and matrix family fails to globally strictly orient KO7 Step, unconditionally or under its stated dominance or positivity premise.

files.summary: Defines the self-nested wrapper chain wrapDouble and proves affine, quadratic, cross-term, multilinear, polynomial, max-plus and projected-primary measures grow unboundedly along it from one positive value. Uses this to discharge explicit unbounded-range hypotheses, proving unconditional strict-orientation impossibility for the duplicating step and global systems, keeping only base-dominance or single-value positivity where needed. Exhibits the identically-zero affine measure to show the nonstrict positivity premise cannot be dropped.
files.conclusion: Growth hypotheses are discharged so strict barriers become unconditional and only load-bearing base-dominance or single-positive-value premises remain.

files.summary: Defines barrier certificates as bundled triples (b, s, n) on which orientation provably fails. Constructs additive certificates from a wrapper chain, compositional certificates from the all-base triple under successor transparency, and affine certificates from a supplied term meeting a computable threshold.
files.conclusion: Additive, compositional and affine measures each admit an explicit barrier certificate triple where orientation fails.

files.summary: Introduces base, successor-pump and wrapper-pump shapes and proves each schema-level witness term has one of these shapes. Shows additive, compositional, affine, quadratic, max-plus and matrix-functional witnesses use a computable bound derived from measure data.
files.conclusion: Every schema-level witness term is definitionally base, a successor chain, or a wrapper chain with a computable bound.

files.summary: Adds relation-valued barrier certificates and builds them for restricted-quadratic, max-plus and weighted functional matrix measures. Each construction selects a successor or wrapper chain at a computable threshold derived from the measure data.
files.conclusion: Restricted-quadratic, max-plus and projected matrix-functional measures each admit an explicit computable barrier certificate.

files.summary: Defines the exact duplicating relation DupStep, the six-member DeclaredDirectFamily, and the CheckedNonOrientationCertificate structure recording evaluator, order, substitution and a proof of order violation. Proves generic soundness that any such certificate refutes global orientation of its relation and of its system, with a system-indexed wrapper. Lifts scalar BarrierCertificate and relational RelationBarrierCertificate objects into checked certificates and supplies extractors for each direct family plus fixed KO7 system adapters, including a closed simpleSize certificate with its non-orientation theorem.
files.conclusion: The closed simpleSize certificate refutes global orientation of the exact KO7 rewrite system by its stored evaluator and order.

files.summary: Defines the declared syntax with proof-bearing inputs for six direct families, plus construction and projection escapes and an explicit outside case for RDRS families. Defines classification into blocked, escape, or outside results and proves every direct method is blocked by its extracted checked certificate, with system-level soundness. Proves the classification is exhaustive over the declared inductive only and that RDRS families including tuple interpretations and semantic labeling classify as outside.
files.conclusion: Every declared direct method is blocked by its extracted checked certificate while RDRS families classify as outside the six-family direct syntax.

files.summary: Introduces a reflected grammar of measures over counter and payload with evaluation, payload monotonicity by structural induction, unbounded payload dependence, and orientation of the duplicating step. Defines syntactic positive-floor and effective-payload certificates with executable checkers and proves the pump barrier that unbounded measures cannot orient. Proves effective certificates imply unboundedness and hence blockage, a payload-section dichotomy yielding payload-blindness as necessary for orientation, an exact equivalence between orientation and payload-blindness plus strict counter response, and incompleteness of the checker on payload times counter.
files.conclusion: Orientation of a grammar measure holds exactly when it is payload-blind with strict counter response, so effective payload dependence blocks orientation while the counter projection orients.

files.summary: The file introduces AttainedValueFamily, a carrier of source and target Nat readings with orientation meaning target below source at every index, and adapters grammarFamily and schemaFamily that translate grammar measures and schema evaluations into this carrier while preserving and reflecting orientation. It proves a reusable coefficient-gap dominance lemma and counter monotonicity of MeasureExpr, showing one grammar expression cannot realize both frozen source and target sections when a strict reversal holds. For additive, affine, restricted-quadratic, cross-term, multilinear, polynomial and max families it freezes source and target sections at the base and proves each cannot orient the duplicating step under unboundedness and stated side conditions, and packages all seven with their hypotheses in ReflectedScalarFamilyGrammar whose every constructor fails to orient.
files.conclusion: Every constructor of ReflectedScalarFamilyGrammar with its stored unboundedness and domination hypotheses fails to orient the duplicating step.

files.summary: Defines weak orientation and vector measures with orders dominated by scalar projections. Proves nonstrict orientation already forces payload-blindness and lifts this through dominated scalarizations to componentwise, primary-first, and weighted-sum orders. Combines scalar strict, scalar weak, and vector dominated results into an unconditional direct-measure barrier.
files.conclusion: Strict, weak, and dominated vector orientations of the duplicating step all force payload-blindness, so payload-reading blocks orientation.

files.summary: Shows PrimaryFirstLt allows secondary decreases on primary ties and has explicit two-cycles in dimension three and in every dimension at least three, hence is not well-founded. Constructs prefix-equality lexicographic order and strict-primary weak-remaining order as well-founded repairs dominated by primary, fixed-coordinate, and row-sum projections. Transfers payload-blindness barriers to these orders with counter-vector orientation examples showing non-vacuity.
files.conclusion: Primary-first orders fail well-foundedness in dimension at least three while lexicographic and strict-primary weak orders are well-founded and inherit payload-blindness with non-vacuous counter examples.

files.summary: This file does not prove a new barrier theorem; it closes the co-rewrite and co-WPO note using already-landed scope facts. It defines the packed certificate structure CoRewritePairBoundary recording the notes-table status, the out-of-scope co-order fact, and the generalized-WPO compatibility. It proves the residual row coRewritePairCoWPO is classified as nonconservative_escape and that the co-order scope is not in the direct scope. Its final theorem assembles these into co_rewrite_pair_boundary_closed, with a stable string anchor for auditing.
files.conclusion: Co-rewrite pairs and co-WPO are closed as mere scope escapes, not loopholes in the direct orientation barrier.

files.summary: The file defines additive, abstract combining-function, and affine constructor-local measures with app positivity and subterm laws. It proves none of them can orient the duplicating rec_succ rule or full Step under transparent-delta or unboundedness hypotheses. It defines a delta-depth counter projection that does orient rec_succ while violating both app subterm laws, and packages simpleSize, tau, nodeCount and linear weights as additive instances.
files.conclusion: No additive, transparent-delta abstract, or positive-sensitive unbounded affine compositional measure orients rec_succ or full Step, while the delta-depth counter projection does.

files.summary: This file collects theorem-level barriers for concrete method families. It defines a global-orientation interface and measures including nesting depth, multiplicative polyMul, node count, head precedence, linear weight and tree depth. It proves each cannot orient full kernel Step, with rec_succ and merge_cancel as witnesses, and notes full LPO and MPO succeed so only weaker components are refuted.
files.conclusion: None of the listed simple measures globally orients full kernel Step.

files.summary: This file lifts direct root-step barriers to the full context closure StepCtxFull. It defines global orientation of StepCtxFull and proves any such orienter restricts to the root relation via the identity context. It derives eleven context-closed no-orientation theorems for additive, transparent, affine, quadratic, matrix, multilinear, max and mixed families.
files.conclusion: All eleven listed barrier families survive from root Step to full context closure StepCtxFull.

files.summary: This module supplies six missing context-closed counterparts for three arctic and three Endrullis-Waldmann-Zantema families. Each lift uses the same identity-context bridge, so an orienter of StepCtxFull is in particular an orienter of the root relation. No hypothesis is added or dropped and the file uses only Mathlib.
files.conclusion: The six arctic and EWZ barriers lift unchanged to StepCtxFull.

files.summary: This module completes the context-closed layer by lifting every remaining root no-orientation theorem. It covers affine, arctic, tropical, constellation, flag, kappa, linear, matrix, max, MPO, multilinear, polynomial, quadratic, simpleSize, depth and WPO families via the identity-context bridge. Together with the eleven prior lifts it covers all eighty root barriers with Mathlib only.
files.conclusion: The full remainder lifts so all eighty root barriers hold for StepCtxFull.

files.summary: This module lifts 26 root-level orientation impossibilities with discharged growth premises to the full context closure StepCtxFull. Each statement keeps exactly the premises of its root source; the lift adds nothing because every root contraction is a contextual contraction under the identity context. Families covered include affine, quadratic, multilinear, polynomial, max, arctic, tropical and many matrix and natural-matrix orders. Root and context-closed inventories stay in step at 106 and 106.
files.conclusion: All 26 pump-discharged root orientation impossibilities lift unchanged to the full context closure StepCtxFull, keeping root and context-closed inventories at 106 each.

files.summary: The file defines a KO7 max-aggregative depth family with per-constructor bumps and positivity of the app bump. It evaluates by adding bumps to maxima over arguments. It forgets KO7-only weights to view the family as a schema-level measure. It deduces that no such measure globally orients steps and that standard tree depth in particular does not.
files.conclusion: No KO7 max-depth measure globally orients all steps, and in particular standard unit tree depth does not.

files.summary: The file defines a schema-level max-aggregative depth family with equations for succ, wrap and recur plus a positive wrap offset. It proves no such measure strictly orients the duplicating rule uniformly. The contradiction uses base, succ base and base where both sides share frozen branches. It lifts the result to global orientation without an unbounded-range hypothesis.
files.conclusion: No schema-level max-depth measure strictly orients the duplicating rule uniformly, hence none globally orients a duplicating system.

files.summary: The file records the direct-orientation barrier scope as a nine-field record plus an InScope predicate. It provides a fully true sentinel that is in scope as a positive control. It provides six sentinels for sharing, binders, innermost-only, co-orders, computability and quotients. Each flips exactly one field to False and is proved not in scope.
files.conclusion: The fully true scope is in scope while six sentinels each violating exactly one condition are provably not in scope.

files.summary: The file packages tool-facing fragments for additive, affine, restricted quadratic, bounded multilinear and bounded polynomial measures. Each carries its measure plus explicit unbounded, successor-pump, wrap-pump or dominance witnesses. For each of the thirteen fragments it proves the existing schema barrier forbids global orientation. Unrestricted nonlinear families without witnesses and cross-term and matrix continuations stay open.
files.conclusion: All thirteen tool-facing fragments with their stated witnesses are blocked from global orientation, while unrestricted nonlinear families without witnesses stay open.

files.summary: The file defines a generic direct whole-term observer with carrier, evaluation, visibility, sensitivity and a certificate linking orientation to payload-count drop. It proves an observer seeing a pumped strictly exposed coordinate cannot globally orient the family. It opposes the family rise against the observer-forced drop. It instantiates the payload-count observer and derives its failure.
files.conclusion: No visible carrier-sensitive observer on a pumped strictly exposed coordinate globally orients the family, in particular not the payload-count observer.

files.summary: The file settles the three remaining dominance premises for bounded cross-term quadratic, multilinear and polynomial barriers. It shows each premise follows from wrap positivity alone when the recursor is uncoupled from the counter. It presents one compiled weight with a cross monomial that belongs to all three classes and strictly orients the step. This proves each premise necessary and sharp.
files.conclusion: The three dominance premises are free on uncoupled subclasses and necessary in general, witnessed by one cross-coupled weight that orients the step while violating all three.

files.summary: The file packages hypotheses for three direct scalar families and specializes imported barrier theorems to those packages. It defines bounded cross-term quadratic, max-plus, and WPO-polynomial fragments with unbounded, successor-pump, wrap-pump, or dominance witnesses. It proves each packaged fragment cannot globally orient, and that WPO escape requires failure of base dominance.
files.conclusion: All packaged unbounded or pump fragments are blocked from global orientation, and WPO escape requires base-dominance failure.

files.summary: This file evaluates the carrier-free least-lift law on the Church prefix of System T. It defines the finite subtype Prefix n with its finiteness facts, the restricted type observer obs and cost target cost, and proves the prefix has n plus one values, constant observation, and injective cost. It proves the fiber multiplicity is n plus one and the least licensing lift is n plus one with optimality, then bridges the ambient ChannelLicenses predicate to Licensed on the subtype to obtain the least-cardinality law and its equality with the direct statement. It closes with the n equals four instance and the transfer of the attained channel.
files.conclusion: The Church-prefix count n plus one is the instance of the general least-lift equals fiber-multiplicity law, hence the least licensing channel size.

files.summary: This file proves the channel-capacity law for Church-cost licensing on finite Church prefixes. It defines churchPrefix, the licensing predicate ChannelLicenses, and the syntactic recognizer and index channels. It proves distinct Church applications, the prefix cardinality and typing, that licensing implies injectivity, the lower bound n plus one on any finite licensing channel, impossibility below capacity, attainment with n plus one values, and the least-cardinality characterization. It adds floor-logarithm corollaries and closes finite instances by computation.
files.conclusion: n plus one is the least finite channel cardinality licensing Church-prefix cost, attained by the index channel.

files.summary: This file proves confluence of full System T reduction by Tait-Martin-Lof parallel reduction and Takahashi complete development. It develops shift and substitution algebra, defines the parallel relation Par and the development function dev, and proves reflexivity, shift closure, substitutivity, and the Step-Par-StepStar correspondence. It proves the Takahashi triangle, the parallel diamond, confluence of StepStar, and uniqueness of normal forms when they exist. It exhibits a concrete two-redex fork with distinct one-step reducts joining at succ zero. It proves no termination claim.
files.conclusion: Full System T reduction is confluent with unique normal forms when they exist, witnessed non-vacuously by a two-redex fork joining at succ zero.

files.summary: This file reduces the halting problem to extensional equality of closed System T terms of type nat to nat. It defines the constant-zero term zeroFn, the joinability predicate ExtEqNat, and the primitive-recursive halt-step indicator, and proves numerals are normal and rigid. It proves a representing term equals zeroFn exactly when the represented function is identically zero, that haltStep is primitive recursive and tracks halting, and hence that equality against zeroFn on the represented haltStep family is not a computable predicate. It proves a conditional lift to term pairs under Primcodable and a computable representing map, which are not derived here, plus non-vacuity computations.
files.conclusion: Extensional equality of closed System T nat-to-nat terms against zero is not computable, conditionally lifting to term pairs only under an explicit computable encoding.

files.summary: This file proves the indexed-license boundary for the System T Church family. It defines the syntactic Church index, the retained Church family, the indexed observer, and a subterm occurrence count. It proves the plain type observer fails at fuel at least three, the indexed observer licenses for every fuel, and no fixed finite side channel licenses the full family at the corresponding fuel. It proves singleton retention is licensed while two distinct Church terms with covered costs are not, and that the first Church beta substitution duplicates the successor function exactly n times.
files.conclusion: Indexing by the syntactic Church number licenses Church-family cost where plain and finite observations fail, with exact duplication count n after the first beta step.

files.summary: This file proves three finite results about barriers and observation. It shows on Prefix n the type-observer deficit and its closure to zero under the Church-index channel. It defines coordinate and combined probes on Bool times Bool and proves the two-field set is irredundant while a single combined probe suffices, so irredundancy does not imply minimality. It defines a four-state target and update step and proves two labels suffice one-shot, no two-label observer is updateable, and a three-label observer is, giving the one-shot versus updateable separation. Finite claims close by decidable computation.
files.conclusion: Bounded Church gap closes under the index, irredundancy does not imply minimality, and one-shot reading separates from updateable monitoring by one label.

files.summary: The file defines n-ary System T types, application spines, numeral vectors and the representation predicates RepresentsN and Represents. It proves that zero, successor, projections, composition and primitive recursion preserve representability and combines them by induction on Nat.Primrec' to show every pairing-free primitive recursive function has a closed well-typed representative. It derives the unary corollary for Nat.Primrec functions and exhibits an explicit addition term with a decide-checked 2+3 normalizer fixture.
files.conclusion: Every pairing-free primitive recursive function, and in particular every unary primitive recursive function, is represented by a closed well-typed System T term.

files.summary: The file restates the Church-prefix capacity result on the subtype Prefix n with type observer obs and cost target cost. It computes the fixed-width code deficit as ceiling log2 and the hidden-progress logarithm, and under the uniform prior proves the linear repair curve for k-valued side channels with attainment by initial segments and zero at capacity. It proves the Bayes-risk floor for type-only decoders with attainment by the constant cost decoder and shows the indexed observer and Church index license cost on the Church family while the plain type is their garbling.
files.conclusion: On the Church prefix the type observer needs ceiling log2 bits, any k-valued lift refuses at least 1 minus k over n plus 1 attaining zero at capacity, and type-only decoders err with least refused mass n over n plus 1, while the indexed observer and Church index license cost and type is their garbling.

files.summary: The file builds explicit denumerable and primcodable encodings of System T types and terms and shows successor, application and numerals are primitive recursive. It defines the binary bounded-halting indicator haltStep2, proves it primitive recursive, chooses a closed representative U and defines the computable code-to-term map codeTerm by applying U to the code numeral. It proves codeTerm is typed, represents bounded halting and is computable, then feeds it to the L7a undecidability theorem to obtain unconditional undecidability of extensional equality of nat to nat terms.
files.conclusion: There is a computable map from partial-recursive codes to closed System T terms of type nat to nat representing bounded halting, so extensional equality of such terms is not computable.

files.summary: The file defines simple types, de Bruijn terms, shifting, substitution, full one-step reduction and its closure, normality, the leftmost-outermost strategy with fuelled normalizer and cost, typing and inference, and the Church numeral family with successor and numerals. It records decide-checked fixtures for typing and costs of small Church applications. It proves no boundary theorem and serves as the shared carrier imported by the boundary lanes.
files.conclusion: The file defines the shared System T syntax, reduction, typing, inference and Church family with decide-checked fixtures and proves no boundary theorem.

files.summary: The file proves soundness of type inference and types the Church family, then establishes the leftmost-outermost cost formula for Church applications via successor chains. It shows distinct Church terms share the same inferred type but have different costs, so cost does not factor through type, packages the 2 versus 5 instance as a TypedBoundary and shows the type fiber contains arbitrarily large finite sets with distinct costs.
files.conclusion: Simple typing does not determine leftmost-outermost cost on the Church family because all Church applications share type nat but have distinct costs, so cost does not factor through type and the type fiber is unbounded.

files.summary: Defines free-variable and closedness predicates for System T de Bruijn terms and proves terms typed in the empty context are closed. Introduces application-additive binder-transparent variable-constant direct measures and the well-typed duplicating beta family from (lambda f. f (f zero)) g. Proves orientation is equivalent to every well-typed g evaluating below 2*c, and via a well-typed pump evaluating to 2*c that no such measure orients the family for any c including zero. Exhibits a concrete additive evaluator showing the class is nonempty and a head-variable reader separating Church indices outside the class.
files.conclusion: No typed direct measure orients the well-typed duplicating beta family for any c including zero.

files.summary: This file records explicit counterexamples for several simple measures on KO7 trace syntax. It shows that adding a fixed constant to kappa, a two-component lexicographic pair, a root delta flag, constellation size and additive simpleSize all fail to decrease on the duplicating rec_succ rule. The imported Lex3c safe-step measure is included only as a contrasting certified decrease on a guarded relation.
files.conclusion: Each named simple measure fails to orient the duplicating rule while the imported Lex3c measure orients the guarded safe-step fragment.

files.summary: This file defines a non-duplicating linear recursor step and the additive node-count measure simpleSize. It proves simpleSize strictly orients both linear rules and hence well-foundedness of the linear step relation. It proves by explicit witness that the same measure does not orient the duplicating successor rule, establishing only this contrast.
files.conclusion: Simple node count terminates the linear recursor but cannot orient the duplicating recursor.

files.summary: Repackages the typed recursor barrier as a many-sorted first-order presentation without formalizing a general Aoto-Yamada translation. Defines sorts, terms, iterator and additive and affine measures as abbreviations of the typed versions. Proves the additive barrier and the affine barrier under a step-pump survive unchanged in the many-sorted reading.
files.conclusion: Both additive and pump-backed affine barriers survive as many-sorted barriers.

files.summary: Extends KO7 by one directed collapse rule app t t to t and packages it as a step-duplicating system that still contains the rec_succ duplicating step. Shows the added rule strictly decreases simple additive size and the nonlinear witness W, so every extended step decreases W and the extended root relation is terminating. Proves the additive, transparent-compositional and unbounded-affine global orientation barriers persist unchanged on the extended system.
files.conclusion: The directed first-order collapse surrogate is harmless for termination but does not dissolve any of the existing global barrier classes.

files.summary: Defines payload exposure matrices that store one Nat entry per payload coordinate and term with a certificate equating the entry to the schema payload count. Provides the canonical matrix using the count function itself. Lifts any such matrix to a direct whole-term observer that evaluates the distinguished coordinate with natural order.
files.conclusion: The canonical payload exposure matrix lifts to a direct whole-term observer that reads the distinguished payload coordinate.

files.summary: Develops finite monomial tables over payload-count vectors with cross-coupling and net algebraic dominance conditions that force strict table increase when the target coordinate rises. Builds a direct whole-term observer from dominance data and proves it cannot orient its rule or globally orient its family. Exhibits a cross-coupled dominance inhabitant and a dominance-free two-coordinate escape table and family that globally orients despite duplicating the distinguished payload.
files.conclusion: Dominance forces strict table increase and rules out global orientation, while the dominance-free escape table and family show orientation is possible without it.

files.summary: Defines pure head-precedence measures that rank a term solely by its outermost constructor. Evaluates them via the head-precedence measure. Proves no such family globally orients the step relation, using the collapsing merge_cancel obstruction.
files.conclusion: No pure head-precedence measure globally orients the step relation.

files.summary: Packages the projected-primary dominance pattern where an ambient order forces a designated scalar projection to be nonincreasing while that scalar is an unbounded affine measure. Proves the stronger nonstrict scalar barrier with successor and wrap pump corollaries and the generic dominance theorem with its global version. Specializes back to tracked componentwise and tracked-primary lexicographic vector families.
files.conclusion: Any ambient order dominated by an unbounded affine primary projection cannot orient the duplicating step, covering componentwise and lexicographic vector families.

files.summary: The file models proof-search states with target, known constraints, open obligations, proposal and claim status, and defines consumption of applicable blockers, its persistence along proposal steps, sound audits, self-application gaps and diagnostic-consumption boundaries. It proves that a sound gap refutes consumption, that a reachable gap refutes persistence, and that an explicit trace to a gap or an unsupported promotion yields a first-crossing failure object. It further separates correction discharge from promotion migration, characterizes unsupported promotion and demotion, and shows that a refusal clause makes consumption equivalent to licensing.
files.conclusion: Sound self-application gaps and certified unsupported promotions locate the exact first boundary where diagnostic consumption or licensing is lost and refute persistence along the proposal dynamics.

files.summary: The file specializes schema-level pumped barriers to the concrete KO7 system and schema. For ten measure classes including affine, quadratic, cross-quadratic, matrix pairs, multilinear, max-plus, polynomial, matrix-functional and matrix-mix, it proves no measure globally orients KO7. Each theorem takes the pumped measure as input and applies the corresponding schema theorem.
files.conclusion: No pumped measure in any of the ten listed classes globally orients the KO7 system.

files.summary: The file defines nine schema-generic pumped measure classes carrying explicit successor or wrapper growth witnesses. It proves unconditional duplicating-step barriers for each class and lifts them to global non-orientation for any step-duplicating system. Matrix-functional and matrix-mix cases are reduced to affine pumps through projection and coordinate sums.
files.conclusion: Every pumped class fails to orient the duplicating step and therefore fails globally.

files.summary: The file gives three KO7 specializations of the restricted quadratic counter barrier. It covers the unbounded-range case and the successor-pump and wrapper-pump cases. Each theorem states non-global-orientation for the KO7 system.
files.conclusion: No restricted quadratic counter measure with unbounded range or pump globally orients KO7.

files.summary: The file defines constructor-local quadratic counter measures with an affine successor and wrapper plus a counter-square recursor term. It proves pump lower bounds for successor and wrapper iterates. It proves duplicating-step and global barriers under unboundedness or pump hypotheses, plus non-representability of any global orienter.
files.conclusion: Unbounded or pumped quadratic counter measures cannot orient the duplicating step or any global system containing it.

files.summary: The file gives three KO7 specializations of the bounded cross-term quadratic barrier. Each adds the base-point wrapper-dominance hypothesis to the unbounded, successor-pump or wrapper-pump case. Each concludes non-global-orientation for KO7.
files.conclusion: No bounded cross-term quadratic measure with unbounded range or pump globally orients KO7.

files.summary: The file extends the quadratic barrier with one explicit step-counter cross term under a bounded-coupling regime at the base point. It defines the cross-term measure, unbounded range and bounded-at-base predicates, plus successor and wrapper pump lemmas. It proves duplicating-step and global barriers under unboundedness or pumps together with the boundedness hypothesis.
files.conclusion: Bounded cross-term measures with unbounded range or pump cannot orient the duplicating step or any global system containing it.

files.summary: Defines the semantic projection escape by four pieces adding an explicit collapse factorization to the transaction record. Proves forgetting the collapse gives a transaction escape with transported orientation, well-founded projected relation and factor equality. Proves every escape extends by identity collapse, so four-piece records are inhabited exactly when escapes are.
files.conclusion: Four-piece semantic projection escapes exist exactly when transaction escapes exist.

files.summary: Restates the compositional-impossibility boundary on the four-constructor RecDelta core with schema, embedding and pumping constructors. Defines additive and abstract compositional measures with evaluations and schema views. Proves Tier-1 additive impossibility and Tier-2 transparent-delta impossibility for the duplicating recursor. Gives a counter-depth DP projection that orients the step but violates both app-subterm laws, plus a quadratic witness that orients while breaking transparency. Concludes transparency is essential for Tier-2.
files.conclusion: No additive or transparent-delta compositional measure orients the duplicating recursor, yet DP projection and a nonlinear witness do, so transparency is essential.

files.summary: This file packages a reusable scalar-projection template for vector-valued orientation barriers. It proves that if every R-decrease forces a strict decrease of a scalar projection and that scalar decrease is already impossible on the duplicating step, then R cannot orient the step, with a global-root variant. It then instantiates the template for tracked componentwise pairs via the first coordinate, weighted functional matrix measures via weighted sums, and balanced mixed-coordinate pairs via coordinate sums using unbounded-range scalar barriers.
files.conclusion: No vector-valued measure whose decreases force a blocked scalar decrease can orient the duplicating step.

files.summary: This file develops orientation barriers over ordered carriers. It defines additive measures over partially ordered commutative monoids and compositional measures over preorders, proving that additive orientation is impossible when the successor weight is attained and that compositional orientation is impossible under successor transparency at the base. It shows the attainment hypothesis is necessary via a strictly negative integer model that orients every instance while attaining nothing, and it instantiates the barriers in NatOrdinals with Hessenberg addition plus an affine omega-times-n reading that orients finite payloads but fails at omega.
files.conclusion: Attainability and transparency exactly delimit where ordered additive and compositional orientation barriers apply, with explicit counterexamples beyond the boundary.

files.summary: States constructor-local max-plus equations for succ, wrap and recur with free offsets and zero wrapper scaling. Proves by splitting on the successor offset that the wrapper returns at least its recursive argument, using constancy at zero offset and pumping along successor iteration otherwise. Concludes no such evaluation strictly orients the duplicating step at any offsets.
files.conclusion: Constructor-local max-plus measures at any offsets cannot orient the duplicating step.

files.summary: Packages compiled witnesses for six scope bullets: generic rank-based dependency-pair soundness versus sharp failure of source transport, weak matrix readings with zero orienters, arbitrary weak semantic readings, r-ary duplicator coverage, and a cross-coupled nonlinear weight orienting the step. Proves each bullet with an explicit object, including two distinct KO7 reduction pairs, an empty pair problem versus a non-wellfounded source, and the r-ary quantitative laws at all arities.
files.conclusion: All six scope bullets are backed by compiled witnesses, including nonunique KO7 reduction pairs and a strictly orienting cross-coupled weight.

files.summary: Defines a minimal sharing-aware syntax with a shared application node and a step that references rather than copies the payload. Defines a counter that ignores the shared payload and proves it strictly decreases on the step, giving well-foundedness, so the additive-style direct obstruction disappears under sharing.
files.conclusion: Under sharing the direct counter orients the duplicating step and the reverse step is well-founded, showing the tree assumption is genuine.

files.summary: Derives explicit unbounded-range witnesses from positive successor or wrapper drift for affine, restricted-quadratic and tracked-primary pair measures. Packages each drift hypothesis into the corresponding pumped subclass constructor.
files.conclusion: Positive successor or wrap drift yields explicit unbounded-range witnesses and promotion into pumped subclasses for all three families.

files.summary: Defines the generic step-duplicating schema with base, successor, wrapper and duplicating recursor, plus additive, affine, compositional and projection-rank measures and global orientation. Proves no additive, transparent-successor compositional or unbounded-affine measure can orient the duplicating step or orient a system containing it globally, and that any global Nat orienter is not representable in those classes. Shows projection ranks orient the step while violating wrapper subterm sensitivity, with uniqueness on generated schemas via a shared confession-core and route-evidence layer.
files.conclusion: Direct additive, transparent compositional and unbounded affine measures all fail to orient the duplicating step globally, whereas forgetting projection ranks succeed and are unique on generated schemas.

files.summary: This file instantiates the step-duplicating schema on the textbook rule f of x and successor y to g of x and f of x y with a dummy base. It defines the term syntax, schema view, root step, and packaged system. It proves three barrier corollaries for additive, unbounded affine, and transparent compositional measures. It specializes the generic additive, compositional, and affine witness extractors to this carrier.
files.conclusion: The textbook duplicating rule admits no global orientation by the stated additive, unbounded affine, and transparent compositional measures.

files.summary: This file instantiates every schema barrier at the textbook system across scalar, matrix, arctic and tropical, ordered-carrier, and unconstrained direct families. It defines a cross-coupled weight that strictly orients the rule and packages it as quadratic, multilinear, and polynomial measures violating exactly the dominance premises. It proves those three premises sharp and assembles a full barrier-stack record carried by the textbook rule with an exact boundary theorem.
files.conclusion: The textbook rule carries the full barrier stack, and the three dominance premises are exactly sharp via one orienting cross-coupled interpretation.

files.summary: This file packages the paper-facing fragment coverage ledger over existing wrapper theorems for direct scalar, extended-direct, and matrix-projection families. It defines propositions stating no global orientation for each fragment class and proves them from the fragment theorems. It combines them into a joint coverage catalog, leaving unrestricted nonlinear and matrix classes as residual exclusions.
files.conclusion: All listed direct, extended-direct, and matrix-projection fragments provably fail to globally orient any step-duplicating system.

files.summary: This file closes finite-inventory bookkeeping for the tool-search stack with exact membership, sizes, NoDup, and group counts. It proves the theorem-backed list has fourteen members and the residual list has two, with iff-level catalogs for each list and group. It proves the group-count partition five three six and packages them as an exact inventory proposition with its theorem.
files.conclusion: The theorem-backed list has exactly fourteen deduplicated families split five three six across groups, with two residual families excluded.

files.summary: Packages the paper-facing M4 tool-search surface as a record with certificate, exact inventory, residual boundary and matrix and method closure certificates. Constructs the catalog from upstream layers and projects each component including terminality of residual rows and exact direct and matrix groups. Keeps aggregate matrix rows honest with licensed-escape and not-yet-method statuses and records closure of former FBI and nonlinear rows by theorems.
files.conclusion: The final M4 tool-search catalog projects exact coverage, honest residuals and closed former-residual rows.

files.summary: This file lists every constructor of the theorem-backed and residual family types and proves membership completeness relative to those closed enums. It imports covered and residual statuses with certificate projections and proves each listed family receives its label. It combines them into an audit catalog, noting it does not quantify over external tool-search spaces.
files.conclusion: Every declared family is inventoried with covered status plus certificate or residual status as appropriate.

files.summary: This file refines the grouped status layer into per-family coverage without adding barrier theorems. It defines three fragment groups, assigns each family to a group, and defines coverage by projection to the grouped bundle. It proves the group catalog, projection equalities, and that every family is status-covered and certificate-backed.
files.conclusion: Every theorem-backed family belongs to a fixed group and is covered by its group certificate bundle.

files.summary: This file defines the residual-boundary catalog conjoining covered-family certificates with residual status labels. It proves every theorem-backed listed family has covered status and a certificate and every residual has residual status. It assembles the boundary catalog and shows it follows even with an unused exact-inventory premise without derivation from that premise.
files.conclusion: The boundary catalog conjoins covered-family certificates with residual-only status labels.

files.summary: This file adds a paper-facing status and certificate layer above the coverage ledger without strengthening barrier theorems. It defines covered and residual-exclusion labels, residual families, an exact matrix-residual status split, and a certificate bundling the three theorem-backed bundles. It proves the matrix catalog, certificate construction with projections, and status catalogs, noting residuals are labels not new impossibility theorems.
files.conclusion: The status layer labels every theorem-backed family as covered with a certificate and every residual as residual exclusion with an exact matrix-status split.

files.summary: This file tests whether direct-measure barriers survive in a simply-typed recursor fragment with res, step, and cnt sorts. It defines additive and affine constructor-local measures with a typed step iterator and explicit pump hypothesis. It proves the additive barrier survives outright and the affine barrier survives under an unbounded typed step pump.
files.conclusion: Additive typed barriers hold outright and affine typed barriers hold under an explicit step pump, so simple typing does not escape the barrier.

files.summary: This file is an import-only aggregation root for orientation-boundary and supporting theorem modules. It brings together exactness catalogs, safe-trace certificates, obstruction and complexity material, finite-schema and sharing-boundary APIs, grammar and coverage evidence, and many orientation-closure method modules. It defines no objects and proves no theorems; each imported declaration retains its own statement and trust assumptions.
files.conclusion: As an import-only root with no declarations, the file establishes no mathematical result of its own.

files.summary: The file re-exports schema-oriented modules for step-duplicating schemas, free syntax, textbook instances, dependency-pair fragments, and finite-graph reachability and SCC utilities. It covers canonical traces, confession dominance, norm mismatch, seed factorization, forgetting witnesses, operational incompleteness, witness order, and escape trichotomy. It states no new definitions or theorems beyond the re-exported surface.
files.conclusion: The file adds no theorems and serves only as the conservative primitive and schema-parametric import root.

files.summary: The file is a broad convenience import root for step-duplicating schemas, nonlinear scalar barriers, vector and matrix barriers, symbolic comparators, pump infrastructure, executable witness tooling, textbook instances, confession-method families, dependency-pair fragments, graph SCC utilities, mutual-duplication families, and cross-paper interfaces. It re-exports the listed modules for direct application of any barrier theorem. It states it remains for downstream users but should not be treated as the strict primitive boundary, with KO7-specific certification and complexity results excluded.
files.conclusion: The file proves nothing itself and serves only as the broad convenience import surface for schema barriers.

files.summary: The file extends PrimitiveSchemaAPI with reusable barrier, matrix, mutual-duplication, higher-order sharing, and escape-trichotomy schema modules. It imports schema variants of quadratic, multilinear, polynomial, max, arctic, tropical, depth, ordered-field, LPO, witness, classifier, and call-graph layers. It introduces no new definitions, with the listed modules supplying the extended surface.
files.conclusion: The file adds no theorems and serves only as the extended schema import root over the primitive core.

files.summary: The file checks the CoRewritePairBoundary interface with #check and a paired axiom query for closure. It opens the boundary namespace and asserts the classification that the co-rewrite-pair co-WPO note is a nonconservative escape requiring an out-of-scope co-order. One example re-states that classification; the module anchor records theory-expansion audit.
files.conclusion: The co-rewrite-pair note is classified as a nonconservative escape with closed boundary module.

files.summary: This reach file exercises the DirectBarrierScope layer. It checks that the scope record, InScope predicate and fullScope sentinel elaborate, that fullScope is in scope, and that sharing, binder, innermost-only, co-order, computability and AC-quotient scopes are each out of scope. Every theorem identifier for those exclusions is also checked for reachability.
files.conclusion: The positive in-scope sentinel and all six out-of-scope exclusions type-check.

files.summary: This reach gate audits DirectToolSearchMapping without adding definitions. It checks the thirteen additive, affine, quadratic, multilinear and polynomial fragments with unbounded, successor-pump and wrap-pump search. It also checks the matching no-global-orientation theorem for each fragment.
files.conclusion: All thirteen tool-search fragments are shown without global orientation.

files.summary: This reach file confirms every public name of DirectWholeTermObserver and specializes it to a concrete Bool family. It defines a single-payload single-position schema and family with step from false to true and strict count increase from 1 to 2. It then checks non-orientation of the payload-count observer both through the additive corollary and directly through the main theorem.
files.conclusion: The payload-count observer cannot globally orient the concrete duplicating family.

files.summary: This file reach-checks ten fragment structures for cross-quadratic, max and WPO-polynomial direct tools under unbounded, succ-pump and wrap-pump regimes, including a base-dominance-failure fragment. It checks the corresponding no-global-orientation theorems for each fragment and the escape-requires-failure-of-base-dominance theorem for the last fragment. It proves no new content.
files.conclusion: All extended fragment structures and their no-global-orientation results type-check.

files.summary: This file imports the orientation-boundary API and issues #check and #print axioms commands for direct-measure closure, safe-trace triple-lex exactness, certificate and complexity bridges, audit rows and roadmap closeout catalogs. It contains example proofs that each listed catalog, obstruction carrier, non-surjectivity result and length bound is reachable through this root import. A final example proves the supported-route list has length five and the unsupported-route list has length zero. The file proves no new mathematical content beyond reachability.
files.conclusion: Through this root import every listed orientation-boundary, trace, bridge, audit, closeout and higher-order catalog is reachable and the five-tag supported-route catalog is complete with no unsupported routes.

files.summary: This file checks that seven PrimitiveSchemaAPI names are reachable. It asserts True with a have-reference to projection rank extension, textbook schema, dependency-pair well-foundedness, per-step exchange, factorization criterion, observability equivalence, and direct-escape trichotomy. No new definitions or theorems are declared.
files.conclusion: The file confirms that seven named PrimitiveSchemaAPI declarations are reachable as True witnesses without adding new content.

files.summary: This file checks that every re-exported schema module is reachable through import OperatorKO7.SchemaAPI. It verifies the core additive no-orientation lemma, usable-rules route and convergence-extension equivalences, tropical and max-depth barriers, affine and matrix barriers, fragment coverage and construction certificates, and quantitative seed, forgetting-witness and incompleteness layers. Paired #check and #print axioms commands record each declaration and its axiom footprint.
files.conclusion: The file confirms that the public SchemaAPI exposes the no-orientation barriers and the usable-rules convergence equivalence with their axiom footprints.

files.summary: This file checks reachability through import OperatorKO7.SchemaExtendedAPI. Each True example holds a cited barrier, witness, catalog or boundary declaration so elaboration fails if the import drops it. It covers tropical, fixed-row matrix, arbitrary-matrix and arctic-matrix barriers, mutual-duplication flow barriers, additive witnesses, escape trichotomy, finite-schema catalogs and higher-order lift blockers.
files.conclusion: The file confirms that all extended-API no-orientation, catalog and lift-blocker declarations are reachable.

files.summary: This file checks tool-search fragment exactness and residual boundaries. It issues #check queries for theorem-backed and residual family lists with nodup and length facts, group filters and catalogs, inventories, and boundary catalog implications. Its eight examples assert counts 14 and 2, direct-scalar filtering, membership and grouping facts, residual status, catalog existence, and the complete membership equivalence. It proves no new theory.
files.conclusion: Fourteen tool-search families are theorem-backed and two remain residual with an exact inventory implying the boundary catalog.

files.summary: This file is a reachability check for the final tool-search fragment catalog. It elaborates the catalog construction and its projections to certificates, exact inventories, residual boundaries and matrix and method closure catalogs through paired checks and examples. The examples verify theorem-backed versus residual family membership, terminal status of every method-closure row, closure of two former residual rows, non-universal closure, and exact group and non-overclaim statuses.
files.conclusion: The final catalog projects terminal status to every residual-method row while remaining not universally closed by Lean theorems.

files.summary: This file checks the list-audit surface for tool-search fragments. It verifies completeness of the theorem-backed and residual family lists, covered status with certificates for backed families, residual status for residual families, and elaboration of the audit catalog.
files.conclusion: Theorem-backed families are covered with certificates while residual families carry residual-exclusion status.

files.summary: This file checks the per-family coverage surface. It verifies group projection for direct families, coverage by certificate for matrix families, residual list membership, and covered status for an extended family.
files.conclusion: Direct, extended and matrix families project to their groups with coverage certificates while unrestricted matrix classes remain residual.

files.summary: This file checks elaboration of the fragment-coverage module. It runs checks on the fragment-family type and the direct, extended, matrix and combined coverage catalogs. Its two examples inhabit the family type with extendedMaxPlus and matrixArcticRowSum.
files.conclusion: The fragment-family type is inhabited by extendedMaxPlus and matrixArcticRowSum and its coverage catalogs elaborate.

files.summary: This file checks the residual-boundary catalog. It verifies direct construction of the boundary catalog, covered status with certificate for an extended family, residual status for a nonlinear family, and derivation of the boundary catalog from the exact inventory.
files.conclusion: Covered and residual statuses assemble into a residual-boundary catalog, also obtainable from the exact inventory.

files.summary: This file checks the coverage-status layer. It verifies the coverage-status type, residual families, coverage certificates and their direct, extended, matrix and matrix-residual projections, and the covered, residual and matrix status catalogs including refinement of the exact catalog.
files.conclusion: Covered families map to covered status and unrestricted matrix classes to residual exclusion, with the matrix residual catalog refining the exact catalog.
